comments.body:
I'm not an expert, but I think this only requires adding `defaultText` to the complaining option to get it to pass the failing checks. 

I stumbled on this MR looking for rosec in nixpkgs (after failing to find it at search.nixpkgs.org). I'd love to see this merged once the changes pass ci builds. It looks like a rather good implementation to my (admittedly pretty green) eyes. Thanks for the implementation. I'll try to test it out here shortly. I'm rebuilding my nix config to change the structure, so it may take a bit of time to get there, but it is in my queue of todos.
Login in the nixosTests fails on aarch machines and I have no way to debug that currently. I may rent a arm ec2 or something to test but any help here is appreciated.

I have addressed the aarch failure by marking the test as broken and added a little comment as to why. If in the future if it requires test coverage I will adjust the test to behave conditionally based on the platform and perform correct tty login. For now, I don't think it justifies blocking this PR.

This should be broken into several commits:
- One adding yourself as a maintainer
- One for **each** package
- One for the new module
- One for the PAM changes

@EpicEric Out of pure interest and because I'd like to learn: What good would this do in this case? A revert of this entire commit wouldn't affect backwards compatibility in any way, so I wonder what I am not seeing here. Is it easier to review that way?

The reason I grouped these things together is that the integration test only make sense with all changes together. I suppose it would make sense to add the packages separately.

Per [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-conventions):

> - Create one commit for each logical unit.

This ensures that "others can later understand why a change was made. While this potentially can be understood by reading code, PR discussion or upstream changes, doing so often requires a lot of work".
I must say that "logical unit" is pretty vague, but I will take your advice as reference.

I have split the commit and also rebased solving a small conflict in the PAM module.

Since I could use my original commit as oracle I ran this task with AI and reviewed it.

Does this mean I have to mark every commit as "Assisted-by: OpenCode" even though the actual code was mine only or do I leave it that way?
